investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both are fully consumed, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. The pod remained unscheduled for ~145–147 seconds, exhausting the eval timeout before any VM was assigned, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever written and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" confirms that no schedulable capacity exists and preemption cannot help. Because the pod never starts, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returns a VM-backed agent, and the probe times out without writing any required evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure scoped to the remote-agents Swarm/kata-peerpods node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' and '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' across all 6 nodes, with preemption also unavailable.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message for the remote-agent-runtime check, pod stuck for 145s.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be satisfied without a scheduled VM.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=148130 (~148s) exceeds the pod-stuck duration of 145s, confirming the probe waited the full scheduling window before failing.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: existing remote agent pods or other workloads have consumed all available VM slots, leaving zero capacity for new scheduling requests.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the schedulable pool to those 2 already-exhausted nodes.

Tertiary — node pool not scaled out: the cluster autoscaler has not added new kata-peerpods-capable nodes, either because autoscaling is disabled, the node group has hit its maximum, or the scale-out event has not yet completed.

Quaternary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: previously created agents that were not cleaned up may be occupying VM resource slots without serving traffic, starving new probe pods.

Lower confidence — recent change 574b6b2 'fix(remote-agents): stop polling state of dead/stuck remote agents' touched all three eval source files (features.json, check-expectations.json, run-status-probes.mjs); if this change altered cleanup logic it could affect how stuck pods are released, but no source diff is available to confirm causality.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-25T11:02–11:07Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have zero remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector), causing every new remote-agent pod to remain Unschedulable until the eval timeout is reached. Because no agent pod was ever scheduled, the runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs never reached the state-polling step, so the expected evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were never written and the contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:264 was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the Remote Agents feature (production-api runtime environment) has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across all eligible nodes. Of the 6 nodes in the cluster, 2 carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but report it as Insufficient, and the remaining 4 do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector at all. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. As a result, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for ~145–147 seconds before the eval timed out, preventing agent creation, state polling, and runtime checks from producing any evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; the impact is scoped to this observability eval.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on all eligible nodes: the 2 nodes that carry this resource have no remaining capacity, and the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption victims exist, so the scheduler cannot free capacity automatically. This directly explains the identical Unschedulable message across all three sibling checks.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector. If the selector was recently tightened or node labels were removed, the effective scheduling pool may have shrunk from a larger set to only 2 nodes, making exhaustion more likely. This is a hypothesis; no label-change evidence is present in the packet.

QUATERNARY — Cluster under-provisioned for concurrent eval load: if multiple eval runs or real workloads are competing for the same kata.peerpods.io/vm slots simultaneously, transient exhaustion is possible even without a leak.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both are fully consumed, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. The pod remained unscheduled for ~145–147 seconds, exhausting the eval timeout before any VM was assigned, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever written and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" confirms that no schedulable capacity exists and preemption cannot help. Because the pod never starts, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returns a VM-backed agent, and the probe times out without writing any required evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure scoped to the remote-agents Swarm/kata-peerpods node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' and '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' across all 6 nodes, with preemption also unavailable.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message for the remote-agent-state check, pod stuck for 147s.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message for the remote-agent-runtime check, pod stuck for 145s.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was written, confirming the agent pod never reached a running state.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, matching the scheduler failure preventing pod start.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; if the pod is never scheduled this call cannot complete and no evidence is emitted.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be satisfied without a scheduled VM.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=148130 (~148s) exceeds the pod-stuck duration of 145s, confirming the probe waited the full scheduling window before failing.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: existing remote agent pods or other workloads have consumed all available VM slots, leaving zero capacity for new scheduling requests.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the schedulable pool to those 2 already-exhausted nodes.

Tertiary — node pool not scaled out: the cluster autoscaler has not added new kata-peerpods-capable nodes, either because autoscaling is disabled, the node group has hit its maximum, or the scale-out event has not yet completed.

Quaternary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: previously created agents that were not cleaned up may be occupying VM resource slots without serving traffic, starving new probe pods.

Lower confidence — recent change 574b6b2 'fix(remote-agents): stop polling state of dead/stuck remote agents' touched all three eval source files (features.json, check-expectations.json, run-status-probes.mjs); if this change altered cleanup logic it could affect how stuck pods are released, but no source diff is available to confirm causality.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-25T11:02–11:07Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have zero remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector), causing every new remote-agent pod to remain Unschedulable until the eval timeout is reached. Because no agent pod was ever scheduled, the runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs never reached the state-polling step, so the expected evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were never written and the contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:264 was fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the Remote Agents feature (production-api runtime environment) has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across all eligible nodes. Of the 6 nodes in the cluster, 2 carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but report it as Insufficient, and the remaining 4 do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector at all. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. As a result, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for ~145–147 seconds before the eval timed out, preventing agent creation, state polling, and runtime checks from producing any evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; the impact is scoped to this observability eval.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on all eligible nodes: the 2 nodes that carry this resource have no remaining capacity, and the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption victims exist, so the scheduler cannot free capacity automatically. This directly explains the identical Unschedulable message across all three sibling checks.

If the selector was recently tightened or node labels were removed, the effective scheduling pool may have shrunk from a larger set to only 2 nodes, making exhaustion more likely. This is a hypothesis; no label-change evidence is present in the packet.

QUATERNARY — Cluster under-provisioned for concurrent eval load: if multiple eval runs or real workloads are competing for the same kata.peerpods.io/vm slots simultaneously, transient exhaustion is possible even without a leak.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Exhaustion: kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Insufficient Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: 2 of 6 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the remote agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or collecting any response evidence, leaving all five required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the two nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled (~145–147 s), preventing the eval runner from provisioning a remote agent VM and therefore producing zero evidence output. This is a cluster-level resource exhaustion condition localized to the kata peer-pods VM resource type, not an application code defect.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=151777, status=fail — pod was stuck unscheduled for 145 s before the check timed out
failed-check.evidence: evidence={} — zero evidence keys returned; all five required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing (expected-output.missing-required-evidence)
sibling.remote-agent-create: identical scheduling error message, latencyMs=148130, endedAt=2026-06-25T11:02:04.006Z — confirms the condition existed before the remote-agent-runtime run

sibling.remote-agent-state: same scheduling error (pod stuck 147 s), endedAt=2026-06-25T11:04:35.664Z — all three sequential checks hit the same wall, indicating persistent resource exhaustion rather than a transient spike

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1917-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after acquiring orgId — the pod scheduling failure occurs at this createAgent call, before any evidence can be collected

source.infra/evals/status/features.json:185: remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false, so this failure does not itself constitute a declared outage, but both required sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) also failed
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota exhausted on the two affinity-matching nodes: concurrent or leaked remote-agent pods from prior runs may be holding all available VM slots, leaving none for new scheduling attempts.

Secondary — the two kata-capable nodes are under maintenance, cordoned, or have had their kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource capacity reduced, shrinking the schedulable pool without a corresponding reduction in demand.

Tertiary — the node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes, and those 2 nodes have a low kata.peerpods.io/vm limit (e.g., limit=2) that is fully consumed; a misconfiguration of the limit or the selector could make this condition chronic.

Lower probability — a transient burst of legitimate remote-agent workloads from other tenants consumed all VM slots at the exact time the eval ran; this would be a timing collision rather than a persistent exhaustion.

reproductionSteps.details: Use cluster tooling (e.g., kubectl describe node) on the nodes that match the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector to read the kata.peerpods.io/vm Allocatable and Requests fields.

reproductionSteps.label: List all running or pending pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm on the affected nodes
reproductionSteps.details: Identify whether leaked or long-running remote-agent pods from prior eval runs are holding VM slots that should have been released.

reproductionSteps.details: Look for pods in Pending state with the Unschedulable condition to confirm the scheduling backlog and its age.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — kata peer-pods VM scheduling layer (production-api)
affectedAreas.reason: The Kubernetes scheduler reports Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm on the only two nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector, blocking all remote agent pod creation (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the two kata-capable nodes in the production cluster to read current kata.peerpods.io/vm Allocatable and Requests values and identify which pods are consuming all available slots.
Check for any Pending or Running remote-agent pods that were not cleaned up by prior eval runs; terminate any leaked pods to free VM slots.

Review the withCleanup logic in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (around the remote-agent-runtime branch at line 1916) to confirm that failed or timed-out remote-agent pods are reliably deleted after each eval run, preventing slot leakage.

If VM slot capacity is confirmed exhausted by legitimate workloads rather than leaks, evaluate increasing the kata.peerpods.io/vm limit on the two affinity-matching nodes or adding additional kata-capable nodes to the cluster.

After any remediation, re-run all three remote-agents checks and confirm that evidence keys (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are present and the message assertion ('hello from aura') passes before closing this investigation.

Note that this is an eval infrastructure failure against the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence, so this should not be declared a user-facing outage without additional signals.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion is still present or has self-resolved; a pass would indicate transient exhaustion.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run all three remote-agents checks to assess full feature health
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the shared scheduling failure persists across all checks, confirming cluster-level rather than check-specific failure.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on affinity-matching nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Reading Allocatable vs. Requests for kata.peerpods.io/vm on the two nodes that match the pod selector will confirm whether slots are exhausted or the resource has been removed/zeroed.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the affected nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies leaked or stuck remote-agent pods from prior eval runs that may be preventing new scheduling; if found, terminating them would free capacity and allow a re-run to pass.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the two affinity-matching nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm Allocatable > 0 and Requests = 0, the resource exhaustion hypothesis is wrong and the scheduler message would need a different explanation.

If the remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state checks pass on an immediate re-run without any cluster intervention, the failure was a transient scheduling collision rather than persistent exhaustion.

If the node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod spec was recently changed to exclude the kata-capable nodes entirely (e.g., a misconfigured label), the root cause would be a selector misconfiguration rather than VM slot exhaustion.

If no pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm on the affected nodes, the capacity limit itself may have been set to 0 or the extended resource may have been removed from the node, which would be a configuration change rather than exhaustion by workload.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm Allocatable vs. Requests on all affinity-matching nodes before attempting remote agent creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct 'cluster-capacity' check rather than a timeout.

Add a post-run cleanup verification eval that confirms no remote-agent pods remain in Running or Pending state after each remote-agents eval cycle, catching slot leakage before it causes scheduling exhaustion.

Add a historical trend eval that tracks remote-agent pod scheduling latency over time; a rising p95 scheduling time would give early warning of approaching VM slot exhaustion before checks start failing.

Consider a dedicated 'remote-agent-schedulability' check that probes the scheduler dry-run (e.g., kubectl --dry-run) for a remote-agent pod spec, allowing capacity issues to be detected without actually consuming a VM slot.
